notes: Rabi cereal; classic rotation is cotton-wheat or rice-wheat. Follow with a legume/cotton; avoid cereal-after-cereal.
Kharif cereal; rice-wheat is dominant in Punjab but cereal-cereal depletes soil. Insert a legume (mungbean) when possible.
Heavy feeder; rotate to legumes/oilseeds to restore N and break grass pests.
Drought-tolerant cereal; follow with a legume. Avoid another grass crop next.
Drought-tolerant cereal for arid zones; rotate to pulses to rebuild fertility.
Salt/drought-tolerant Rabi cereal; follow with legume/cotton. Avoid cereal-after-cereal.
Long-duration (12+ months) and ratooned; very heavy feeder. After final ratoon, plant a legume to restore soil; avoid replanting cane without a break.
Kharif cash crop; cotton-wheat is the major rotation. Follow with wheat or a legume; avoid back-to-back cotton (pest/disease build-up).
Rabi pulse (gram); fixes N. Follow with a heavy feeder (cotton/cereal). Avoid pulse-after-pulse.
Rabi pulse (masoor); N-fixer. Rotate to cereals/cotton to use fixed nitrogen.
Short-duration Kharif pulse; excellent N-fixing catch crop between cereals in rice-wheat/cotton systems.
Kharif pulse (mash); N-fixer. Follow with a cereal/cotton. Avoid legume-after-legume.
Rabi oilseed (sarson); rotate to cereals/cotton. Avoid following with another brassica (shared pests).
Spring/Kharif oilseed; rotate to cereals/legumes. Avoid back-to-back sunflower (disease).
Rabi tuber; heavy feeder. Rotate away from potato (and other solanaceae) to break blight/nematode cycles.
